content.title: Sequoia Capital Reports Major Changes, Blindsided by Departed Leader
content.caption: Sequoia Capital, a prominent venture capital firm, announced recent changes including the closure of its London office, the merger of its early-stage and growth teams, and the end of its Scouts program. A report from the Financial Times claims these changes are an attempt to undo the legacy of former leader Roelof Botha, who stepped down as the firm’s steward last year.

slides.heading: Impact of Changes
slides.text: Sequoia’s partners were blindsided by the announcement, as Botha didn’t ask for compliance or sign off from the partnership, even though his new role could complicate the firm’s ability to trade its $20 billion stake.
